conventions.convention: The spin alphabet is finite and nonempty, sites are enumerated bijectively starting at x₁, and local weak convergence tests every finite-coordinate marginal on the cylinder sigma-algebra.

Counting measures are Borel measures on Euclidean space, allow repeated atoms and the empty measure, and have finitely many atoms with multiplicity on every compact set. Vague convergence tests nonnegative continuous compactly supported functions.
Generators have nonnegative off-diagonal entries and zero row sums; they act on column observables, while row probability vectors evolve by right multiplication.

Uniformization uses q=maxᵢ λᵢ and R=I+L/q when q>0, includes self-transitions, and uses exponential waiting times independent of the embedded chain. When q=0 the process is constant. The construction filtration records counts and states and is neither completed nor made right-continuous.

The maximal bound assumes Choice and an all-pairs square-integrable martingale with M₀=0 and a measurable probability-one càdlàg event. Its measurable supremum is defined over nested dyadic grids including T and agrees with the full path supremum on that event.

Relative entropy uses natural logarithms, strictly positive reference probabilities, omitted zero-weight terms, and omitted conditional terms on zero-mass blocks. Empty and full event groupings have binary divergence zero.

A continuous predictable bracket belongs to the class of continuous predictable increasing processes B with B₀=0, integrable terminal value, and M²−B a martingale; uniqueness is indistinguishability within this class.
The example uses a different finite probability space for each n and asserts convergence in probability separately for each vague test, without requiring a common coupling.

load_bearing.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Every rate matrix on a nonempty finite state set and initial probability vector admit a uniformized realization with càdlàg nonexplosive paths and conditional transitions P(X_t=j | F_s)=(e^{(t−s)L})_{X_sj} for every 0≤s≤t, where F_s records event counts and states through s.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. For a finite-state rate matrix L, its uniformized realization X, and bounded real f, M_t=f(X_t)−f(X₀)−∫₀ᵗLf(X_s)ds is a square-integrable martingale on every finite horizon. Its continuous predictable bracket is A_t=∫₀ᵗ[L(f²)−2fLf](X_s)ds, and M²−A is a martingale.

Under Choice, a real square-integrable all-pairs martingale on [0,T] with M₀=0 and a measurable probability-one càdlàg event has measurable dyadic supremum S_T agreeing there with the path supremum, and E[S_T²]≤4E[|M_T|²].

For a finite nonempty discrete alphabet S, Ω=S^{ℤᵈ} carries the product topology and cylinder sigma-algebra. Local weak convergence of probability measures means convergence of every finite-coordinate marginal.

For a finite nonempty totally ordered alphabet and a bijective site enumeration, the metric ρ(σ,η)=Σₖ≥₁2^(−k)1_{σ_{xₖ}≠η_{xₖ}} induces the product topology; the configuration space is compact, its Borel and cylinder sigma-algebras coincide, and finite-marginal convergence is equivalent to convergence of integrals of every bounded continuous real function.

For probability vectors P,Q on finite nonempty I×J with Q strictly positive, D(P‖Q)=D(P_X‖Q_X)+Σ_{x:P_X(x)>0}P_X(x)D(P_{Y|x}‖Q_{Y|x}). Grouping atoms into any event C and its complement gives D(P‖Q)≥d(P(C)‖Q(C)), with the stated endpoint and conditional-law equality criteria.

published_dependencies.used_for: Finite nonempty lattice alphabet and configurations as functions on ℤᵈ in the local-topology definition.
Explicit Choice assumption for conditional-expectation interfaces and the countable sequence construction used in uniformization.
Adaptedness, all-pairs martingale identities, square integrability, and the absence of completeness or right-continuity assumptions on filtrations.
Predictable rectangle generators and preservation of predictability under pointwise limits, used for continuous bracket left-step approximations.
Conditional linearity, order, modulus bound, and expectation identities in the maximal and finite-chain martingale proofs.
Bounding E[|M_T|S_n] in the finite-grid L² maximal inequality.
Tail integration of the finite-grid maximum squared.
Interchanging nonnegative tail and probability integrals in the maximal inequality.
Passing from nested finite-grid maxima to the dyadic supremum and obtaining probability continuity in the nonexplosion argument.
Nonnegativity and exact zero criterion for finite relative entropy, including conditional divergences in event grouping.
Positive-domain natural logarithm convention in the entropy chain rule.
Splitting logarithms of joint-to-reference probability ratios into marginal and conditional ratios.
Restricting the enlarged uniformization-history conditional transition law to the construction filtration and conditioning subdivision increments.
Removing the bounded adapted factor M_u from conditional expectations of martingale increments in the bracket proof.
Constructing the countable joint sequence of embedded states and independent exponential waiting times from explicit measurable kernels under Choice.
Extending finite-prefix factorization from generating cylinder events to independence of the full embedded-state and waiting-time sequences.
Interchanging bounded time and event integrals when identifying the finite-chain generator martingale drift.
Uniqueness of continuous predictable increasing brackets: their difference is a continuous martingale whose total variation has an integrable bound.
